overview: 52 official Qs (2008, 2017, 2019, 2025). Two blocks carry it: constitutional bodies (18 – Finance Commission, CAG, ECI, UPSC, SC/ST commissions, 'which is constitutional') and Union-State relations (27 across legislative lists, legislative, administrative and financial relations). RTI, Lokpal/Lokayukta and NHRC give 7 together. Formats: one-liners on 'which List / which Article / who appoints', many negative stems, and 2025 statement-based and count questions.

possibility.angle: Distribution of legislative powers: the three Lists, residuary
possibility.what_they_ask: which List holds a subject (education, planning, opium, banking, High Courts, mineral-rights tax); Art 248 residuary with Parliament; limits on Parliament (distribution of powers).
natural targets: Art 73 (Union executive power extends to Union List matters) vs Art 162 (State), Art 258 (Union entrusting functions to States), Art 258A (States to Union).

possibility.angle: Legislative relations: Parliament on State subjects, repugnancy
possibility.what_they_ask: Art 249 (RS resolution 2/3 present and voting), 250 (emergency), 252 (two or more States), 253 (treaties, no consent needed); Concurrent vs State conflict; doctrine of paramountcy.

possibility.angle: Administrative relations: directions, All-India Services, co-operation
possibility.what_they_ask: consequence of ignoring Union directions (Art 256/257 → 365 → 356); AIS vs Central services (IAS, IPS, IFoS only are AIS); removal of AIS officers by the Union; Art 263 Inter-State Council.

possibility.angle: Financial relations: Finance Commission shares, funds, taxes, loans
possibility.what_they_ask: FC tax-share percentages (10th 29%, 14th 42%); who recommends distribution; Art 266 Consolidated Fund; Art 276 profession tax cap Rs 2,500; Art 293 loans to States; Art 354 during emergency.

possibility.angle: Constitutional bodies: FC, CAG, ECI, UPSC, SC/ST commissions, AG
possibility.what_they_ask: constitutional vs statutory vs executive status; Article numbers (280, 148, 324, 315, 338, 350B); appointment by the President; terms (CAG 6 yrs/65); composition (FC chairman + 4; ECI 3); functions in 'all correct except' form; first chairpersons.
year constituted (1993, PHRA 1993); natural neighbours: statutory status, chairperson a former CJI/SC judge, selection committee.
predecessor law (Freedom of Information Act 2002); selection committee for State CIC (CM, LoP, a Cabinet Minister – no judge); objectives (transparency, accountability).
Lokpal Act 2013 in force 16 Jan 2014; first State Lokayukta (APPSC key: Maharashtra); first AP Lokayukta (Justice A. Sambasiva Rao, 1983).

traps.trap: Swaps the List of a subject [Union / State / Concurrent]
traps.spot: Subject that was moved (education) or sounds 'national' or 'local'
traps.fix: Education → Concurrent since 42nd Amd 1976; economic and social planning → Concurrent; banking, opium, High Courts' organisation → Union; public health, agriculture, land, water → State; mineral-rights tax → State (Entry 50).
traps.pyq: 'Education is included in ___ List' → Concurrent [group2-2008-paper2#112]; 'not in the State list' → Higher education [prelims-2019#58]; High Courts → Union, mineral rights tax → State [mains-2025-paper1#104]

traps.trap: Gives a power reserved to the Rajya Sabha to the Lok Sabha
traps.spot: Statement-based list of when Parliament can legislate on State List
traps.fix: Art 249 resolution is passed only by the Rajya Sabha (2/3 present and voting).
traps.pyq: 'The Lok Sabha passes a resolution ... authorising Parliament' → the false statement [mains-2025-paper1#107]

traps.trap: Labels a statutory or executive body as constitutional
traps.spot: 'Which is not a constitutional body' / 'how many are constitutional'
traps.fix: Constitutional: FC 280, CAG 148, ECI 324, UPSC 315, NCSC 338, NCST 338A, NCBC 338B (since 2018), Special Officer Linguistic Minorities 350B, Inter-State Council 263. Statutory: NHRC, NCM, CIC, Lokpal. Executive: Planning Commission, NITI Aayog.
traps.pyq: Only Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is constitutional → 1 [mains-2025-paper1#97]; Planning Commission → not constitutional [group2-2008-paper2#141]

traps.spot: Statement naming CJI, PM or Parliament as appointer
traps.fix: President appoints the CEC/ECs, FC, UPSC members, CAG; Governor appoints State CIC on a CM-LoP-Minister committee.
traps.pyq: 'CEC is appointed by the Chief Justice' → false [mains-2025-paper1#96]; State CIC committee includes HC Chief Justice → false [mains-2025-paper1#102]

traps.trap: Gives a body a function it does not have
traps.spot: 'All correct except' on functions of FC or CAG
traps.fix: FC only recommends (tax shares, grants principles, referred matters) – it keeps no accounts. CAG audits Union AND State accounts; it does not control the financial system.
traps.pyq: 'Maintains the income and expenditure details' → not an FC function [mains-2017-paper2#127]; CAG 'related to the Union government only' → wrong [mains-2017-paper2#113]

traps.fix: 280 Finance Commission (290 is pension adjustments); 292 Union borrowing, 293 State borrowing and Union loans to States.
traps.pyq: 'Article 290 provides for the FC' → incorrect [mains-2025-paper1#122]; loans to States → Article 293 [mains-2025-paper2#19]

traps.trap: Reverses the direction of an emergency financial power
traps.spot: 'President can ... the transfer of finances' with reduce/cancel/increase
traps.fix: Art 354: during National Emergency the President may reduce or cancel transfers to States – never 'increase' as an emergency power.
traps.pyq: 'Increase the transfer of Finances from Centre to States' → the exception [mains-2017-paper2#117]

traps.trap: Misplaces a service between All-India and Central
traps.spot: IFS abbreviation; removal powers over AIS officers
traps.fix: AIS = IAS, IPS, Indian Forest Service. Indian Foreign Service is a Central Service. AIS members are removable only by the Union.
traps.pyq: Indian Foreign Service → Central Service [group2-2008-paper2#142]; AIS removal → only by the Union [mains-2017-paper2#98]

techniques.name: Status sort [constitutional / statutory / executive]
techniques.how: Before reading options, tag each body by origin: Article number? → constitutional; an Act? → statutory; a Cabinet resolution? → executive. Then count or eliminate.
techniques.example: NITI Aayog (resolution 2015) executive; NCM (1992 Act) and NHRC (1993 Act) statutory; Special Officer (Art 350B) constitutional → answer 1 [mains-2025-paper1#97]

techniques.name: Escalation chain for Union directions
techniques.how: Remember the chain: Art 256/257 directions → non-compliance → Art 365 presumption → Art 356 President's Rule. Options jumping to National Emergency or police deployment fall.
techniques.example: State ignores Union administrative directions → Art 365 → 356 → 'President can declare a Constitutional Emergency in the State' [mains-2017-paper1#103]

techniques.name: Finance Commission number line
techniques.how: Anchor the share by Commission: 10th 29% (gross revenues), 13th 32%, 14th 42%, 15th 41%. Match the Commission in the stem to the line.
techniques.example: 14th FC → 42%; 32.5% and 29.5% are distractors near the 13th and 10th figures → 42% [prelims-2017#101]

techniques.name: Article 249–253 grid
techniques.how: For 'Parliament on State List' multi-picks, tick: 249 RS resolution, 250 emergency, 252 two or more States consent, 253 treaty (no consent). Any statement changing the House or adding consent is false.
techniques.example: A (two or more States), B (RS 2/3), C (international agreements) true; D (Lok Sabha resolution) false → A, B and C only [mains-2025-paper1#107]

techniques.name: Assertion-reason: status vs function
techniques.how: When R gives a body's status and A gives its function, ask whether status causes the function. Usually the function flows from a separate Article.
techniques.example: UPSC is central recruiting agency (A) and an independent constitutional body (R): both true, but recruitment flows from Art 320 → R is not the explanation [mains-2025-paper1#109]

confusions.remember: 249 = Rajya Sabha decides; 252 = States request, law applies only to consenting States.
253 needs no State consent at all.
India follows Canada: residuary with the Centre; Entry 97 List I.
280 FC; 290 pension adjustments; 293 State borrowing and Union loans to States.
All revenues and loans → CFI; other public money → Public Account; Contingency Fund = imprest at the President's disposal.
Union highest law officer vs its State counterpart.
Only IAS, IPS, IFoS are All-India Services.
338A split by 89th Amd 2003; 338B by 102nd Amd 2018 – NCBC was statutory in 2017.
Planning/NITI are executive bodies; FC is constitutional (Art 280), quasi-judicial, advisory.
CAG 6 years or 65 (longest tenure); others 5 years.
Bill passed Dec 2013, assent 1 Jan 2014, commencement 16 Jan 2014.
Paramountcy settles a conflict on the same Concurrent matter in favour of the Union law.

anchors: Seventh Schedule: List I Union, List II State, List III Concurrent
42nd Amd 1976 moved education (and forests, weights and measures etc.) to Concurrent
Art 246 Lists; Art 248 residuary with Parliament
Art 256–257 directions; Art 263 Inter-State Council; Art 365 non-compliance
Art 266 CFI; Art 276 profession tax cap Rs 2,500; Art 280 FC; Art 293 loans to States; Art 354 emergency finance
Art 148 CAG – 6 years / 65, salary of SC judge
Art 315–316 UPSC – members appointed by the President
Art 324 ECI – three members since 1993, equal powers, majority decisions
Art 338 NCSC, 338A NCST, 338B NCBC, 350B Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
RTI 2005 replaced FoI Act 2002; State CIC committee: CM, LoP, a Cabinet Minister
Lokpal Act 2013 in force 16 Jan 2014; AP Lokayukta 1983 (Justice A. Sambasiva Rao)
checklist: Subject question: is it a moved subject (Concurrent since 1976) or a classic Union/State entry?
Body question: tag constitutional / statutory / executive by its Article or Act.
Who appoints? President (Union bodies), Governor (State bodies) – never CJI or Parliament alone.
Which House? Art 249 power is the Rajya Sabha's.
Near-number options (280/290, 292/293): recall the exact Article.
Negative stem: the false option usually widens or reverses a body's function.
